questions: Is the swollen area painful, warm/red, and does it start after an injury or insect bite?
Does the swollen area have any visible redness or warmth to the touch?
Does the swollen area feel warm or look red compared with the surrounding skin?
Can he walk or bear weight on that foot, or does the pain prevent it?
Does the foot swelling involve the whole area or is it centered over a single joint, and can you tell which joint (e.g., ankle or toes) hurts most?
Does he have a fever (temperature ≥ 38.0°C/100.4°F) or does he seem ill?
Can he fully move his ankle and toes through normal range of motion, or does movement of the ankle/foot significantly worsen the pain?
Did the child have any recent injury or activity that could have caused a foot/ankle sprain or fracture (e.g., running/jumping, twisting, fall)?
Is the skin over the swollen area noticeably red or warmer than the surrounding skin when you compare them side-by-side?
Does he have any point tenderness directly over a bone (e.g., when you press the ankle/foot bones—such as the malleoli, navicular, or base of the 5th metatarsal)?
answers: Yes, it’s painful, and the pain feels kind of sharp and heavy. I don’t know about warm/red, and I don’t think it started after an injury or an insect bite.
I don’t really know if it’s warm or red on the outside. I mainly notice the swelling and the pain.
I can’t really tell if it feels warm or if it looks red compared to the other skin. I mainly notice the swelling and the pain.
He can still try to walk, but it’s painful. It seems like the pain is preventing him a little, but he isn’t completely unable to put weight on it.
It’s mostly on the top and sides of the foot rather than one single spot. I think the ankle area hurts the most, not the toes.
No, I don’t think he has a fever, and he doesn’t seem very ill—more like just the swelling and pain.
He can move his ankle and toes, but moving the foot makes it worse. It does significantly worsen the pain when he moves it.
No, I don’t think there was any injury or twisting, no fall, and no special running/jumping that caused it.
No, I can’t say it looks red or is warmer than the surrounding skin. I mainly notice the swelling and the pain.
Yes, when you press on the bones in the foot/ankle area, it’s tender and hurts. I’m not sure which exact bone it is, but it’s in the ankle/foot area.
